title: The Son by Nature and God Who Is True
english: The surviving fragments of Cyril, Archbishop of Alexandria, on the Epistle to the Romans.

“Concerning his Son, who was born of the seed of David according to the flesh” (Romans 1:3). He says that the one born of the seed of David according to the flesh was declared Son of God in power according to the Spirit of holiness by the resurrection from the dead (Romans 1:4). For we too have been declared sons, but not in power; it is rather by way of grace, as those counted worthy of the calling, who gain this by the will of God the Father alone. But with Emmanuel it would not be so; far from it. Even though he was born of the seed of David according to the flesh, and as one of us is reckoned Son of God because of his humanity, he is nonetheless Son in power and in truth, by nature; and through him we too are made sons, since it is indeed true to say that, once we have been enriched with his Spirit through holy baptism, then truly we say without fear of rebuke, “Abba, Father” (Romans 8:15). So, as images stand to their archetype, so we, who are sons by adoption, stand to him whom the Father has attested to be Son by nature, in power, and in truth.

“His eternal power and divinity” (Romans 1:20). How is his eternal power known through creation? Because the things brought into being and called into existence in time have a perishable nature, their Maker must surely be imperishable and eternal. So they will find no defense on the day of judgment.

“Will their unbelief nullify the faithfulness of God?” (Romans 3:3). More honored than the rest are those who were foreknown, who received the law as their tutor (Galatians 3:24), who held promises concerning Christ, who indeed received them, and who were called before the others; for the Savior said, “I was sent only to the lost sheep of the house of Israel” (Matthew 15:24). They also became the firstfruits of those saved through faith. For if some, out of madness, slipped away from believing, God would not on that account, he says, fail to be true. So then, the Father sent the Son from heaven, yet not all believed in him. Because some have become insolent and unbelieving, will God not be true on that account? By no means!

“Let God be true, and every man a liar” (Romans 3:4). That is, let him be thought and spoken of by us as true, and let falsehood be charged, as it were, to every human being. For the divine nature is wholly unchangeable and unalterable, while human nature is badly shaken, and, as far as possibility goes, every man is a liar. For falsehood, as a sin, sometimes overpowers the human mind, and our nature is in some way open to this sickness as well. But of God, who rules over all, it is not right to think or say any such thing. So the charge will be true in this sense: that human nature, that is, the mind, can suffer falsehood.
